name: Zero Breach Toolkit
works_with: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android collections and iPhone backups
short: A free offline check for traces of known mercenary spyware such as Pegasus and Predator on computers and phones.
what: Zero Breach Toolkit looks for published traces of known mercenary spyware on Windows, Mac and Linux computers, Android collections and iPhone backups. It also checks links, emails, files and QR codes, and points out settings left open on your devices. It reads only, makes no network requests during a scan, and says in every report what it could not check.
who: Anyone worried about spyware, especially journalists, activists and people who help them. If you think you are being targeted right now, the README says to contact the Access Now Digital Security Helpline or Amnesty's Security Lab first.
needs: For the Python version: Python 3.8 or newer, no extra packages and no admin rights
For an iPhone: a local backup on your computer
On a Mac: Full Disk Access for Terminal or the app, so it can read Safari

steps.title: Phone backup? Use the browser check
steps.text: Open archivegenocide.com/scan/phone on the computer that holds the backup and choose the backup folder. Nothing is installed and nothing is uploaded.

steps.title: Get the toolkit for a computer
steps.text: There is also a double-click app on the latest release page. The README notes the Python version avoids antivirus warnings because you run the source directly.

steps.title: Download the latest indicator lists
steps.text: Run this from the toolkit folder. It is the only step that uses the internet. Use `python3` on Mac and Linux.

steps.title: Close your browsers and chat apps, then scan
steps.text: A menu opens. Press Enter for the standard check.

steps.title: Check a phone collection or backup
steps.text: Put the folder path in quotes.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `python -X utf8 scan/zero-breach-toolkit.py --quick` for a faster first pass, then read the "What could not be checked" part of the report.

watch: A clean result is not proof you are safe. It only finds spyware someone has already published traces of.

The project is anonymous and the downloadable programs are not code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS will warn you. Running the Python version from source avoids that, and the README shows how to verify a download.
Reports can hold usernames, file paths, browsing details and message excerpts. Keep them out of shared or synced folders.
`--update` contacts the internet to fetch indicator lists and check for a newer version. Scans themselves stay offline.
